scope: LIVE on the camera, firmware 5.02.0.V91, model w71c1. Hook at 0xC03A5490. FHD 12-bit 59.94p, clip \CINEMA\A001_219. Two camera-allocated 4 MiB blocks. Nothing was assembled on the host: the files were pulled off the card and handed straight to LibRaw.
headline: eight frames of a live clip were compressed by the camera's own hardware, given a trailing IFD by the camera, written to the card, and decoded by LibRaw to the same data a stock frame of the same clip decodes to. 1,426,432 bytes against 3,244,544.

the_files.1 to 8: 1,426,432 bytes each; payload at 0x13400 begins ff d8 ff c3
the_files.9 and 10: 3,244,544 bytes, stock -- exactly the probe's bound of eight

the_ifd_the_camera_wrote.checked: the twelve offsets match the twelve SOI markers in the file exactly, and offset_table - ifd_at is 716, which is ifd_size 714 rounded up to a word

decoded.reading: identical. The clip renders almost black because BlackLevel is 1023 and the data sits at 512 -- the STOCK frame renders the same way with the same code, so that is the scene, not the file. An earlier clip with a lit subject rendered correctly from the same path.

the_bug_that_wedged_the_camera_three_tim.what: ifd_at is 0x13400 plus the payload, and the payload is whatever the codec produced -- 1,343,147 on the first run, which put ifd_at at ...3. Every stm in copy_ifd and every str in write_tables then went to an unaligned address.
the_bug_that_wedged_the_camera_three_tim.why_it_is_fatal: ARM's ldm and stm require word alignment whatever SCTLR.A says. An unaligned one on the CinemaDNG writer's own thread is a Data Abort, and the camera stopped answering.
the_bug_that_wedged_the_camera_three_tim.why_nothing_caught_it: the host tool builds the same layout and never sees it: Python has no alignment. Offline verification of the LAYOUT is not verification of the CODE that writes it.
the_fix: ifd_at rounded up to 16 before anything uses it
the table pointer rounded up to 4, because ifd_size is 714 and 714 is not a multiple of four
the cap given 18 more bytes for the two round-ups
the file length taken from count_table, which carries both, rather than re-derived
the_bug_that_wedged_the_camera_three_tim.how_it_was_isolated: the trailer was split into three levels -- none, written but inert, complete -- so one run could tell the copying from the root pointer. Level 1 wedged, which said copying. The operator said from the start that it had to be the trailer itself and was right.
the_bug_that_wedged_the_camera_three_tim.level: L for the wedge, C for the cause, L for the fix working

corrections.what_was_wrong: the first wedge was blamed on the 2000-frame bound leaving the hook armed across clips, and the operator was asked to power-cycle on that reasoning.
corrections.the_truth: the same probe wedged at a bound of 8. The bound was never the cause; the trailer's alignment was.

corrections.what_was_wrong: 'the root pointer is 1,424,256 and the tables imply 1,425,484, a difference of 1,228 against an ifd_size of 714' -- read off the file mid-diagnosis.
corrections.the_truth: a hex arithmetic slip. The root pointer is 1,424,768 and the difference is 716, which is 714 rounded up to a word. The camera's trailer was self-consistent all along.

corrections.what_was_wrong: the first render of a camera-written file was read as a broken decode.
corrections.the_truth: the stock frame of the same clip renders identically. The clip is dark: BlackLevel 1023 against data at 512. The control should have been run before the conclusion.

known_imperfection.what: BlackLevel reads 1024 in our files and 1023 in the camera's own.
known_imperfection.why: the IFD template was built from a frame of clip A001_200, and that tag's value is stored inline in the entry, so it is frozen from the template's frame.
known_imperfection.cost: one unit of black level. No image data is affected: the tile bytes are never touched.
known_imperfection.the_fix: build the template from a frame of the clip being recorded, or read the handful of inline tags off the frame's own IFD at hook time.

what_is_left: losslessness ON THIS PATH. The engine's bitstream was proven lossless on 2026-09-23 against a surviving stock copy, and nothing here touches the tile bytes, but no frame has yet been compressed AND kept alongside its own original.
asynchronous scheduling. This build waits inside the flush call: 13.65 ms against a 16.7 ms period at 59.94p. The asynchronous encode was proven separately on 2026-09-29.
a whole clip. The bound is eight frames.
